title: The universal Dart patchability contract and compatibility matrix
authority: This file is the authoritative row set for the Mutable-AOT program. #64 must consume it rather than maintain a second list, and every later issue reports against these row ids. CONTRACT.md is the human-readable half and adds no rows.
starting_state_note: Every implementation axis in this file is UNMODELED. That is the correct state at MAOT-0: nothing has been built, so nothing is claimed. The value delivered here is the enumeration, the four-axis separation, the boundary, and a gate that refuses a 100% claim -- not progress.

boundaries.title: Native platform source (iOS/Android/macOS/Windows/Linux)
boundaries.rationale: Objective-C/Swift/Kotlin/Java/C++ application and platform code is compiled into the shipped native binary. Changing it is a separate update domain requiring a new native binary.

boundaries.title: Flutter engine and Dart VM C/C++ changes after release
boundaries.rationale: We fork and modify the engine and VM freely BEFORE a release is cut; the shipped native binary is then fixed. Replacing it post-release is not part of this promise.

boundaries.title: Native plugin ABI changes
boundaries.rationale: A plugin's native side is linked into the shipped binary. Dart-side plugin code is in scope; the native ABI it calls is not.

boundaries.title: New native symbols
boundaries.rationale: A patch may not introduce a native symbol that the shipped binary does not export. Dart code that only reaches existing symbols is in scope.

boundaries.title: Asset and shader transport
boundaries.rationale: Delivering non-Dart payloads is an existing separate mechanism. Dart code changes that merely reference already-shipped assets are in scope.

boundaries.title: Store distribution policy
boundaries.rationale: Whether a given patch is permitted by a platform vendor is a policy question, not an engine capability.

boundaries.title: Backend rollout, targeting and delivery service
boundaries.rationale: Getting a validated patch to a device is the control plane's job and already exists. This program owns whether the patch can be represented and installed correctly once it arrives.

exclusion_classes.title: Core-library representation with SDK-fixed layout
exclusion_classes.rationale: The class ships inside the released SDK and its layout cannot change under a fixed native binary. USER STATE HELD IN SUCH OBJECTS IS NOT EXCLUDED -- it is covered by RS-01, which owns existing heap instances. What is excluded is the class's own shape.

exclusion_classes.title: VM code metadata, not observable Dart program state
exclusion_classes.rationale: Descriptor and map structures that describe compiled code. They are regenerated with the code they describe and are not addressable as Dart program state, so they carry no independent patch semantics. They are consequences of RS-04, not rows.

exclusion_classes.title: FFI and native interop objects
exclusion_classes.rationale: These name native memory and native symbols directly. Their patch semantics are governed by the native boundary, not by Dart mutability.

exclusion_classes.title: VM error and unwind objects
exclusion_classes.rationale: These represent a failed execution state rather than a program construct a developer edits. A patch changes the code that produces them; it does not change them.

tier_policy_note: Tier coverage rules live in lib/contract.py TIER_COVERAGE and are enforced by lib/validate.py. `per_row` tiers must have every frozen universe entry named by a row or an exclusion. `blanket` tiers may be claimed wholesale by one row, because the rule genuinely is one rule -- and the blanket is written down here so it is reviewable rather than implied by an absence.

rows.title: top-level function body
rows.expected_post_patch: Every invocation of compute() from any call site, at any optimization level, returns 2. No call site retains the old body.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A body carries no state of its own; a top-level function holds nothing across the transition. State reached BY the body is the field and instance rows' subject, not this one.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: No state shape changes, so there is nothing whose transformation could be ambiguous.

rows.title: static method body
rows.expected_post_patch: C.v() returns 2 from every call site including statically bound and inlined ones.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: The method body holds no state; the class's static fields are RS-10.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: No state shape changes.

rows.title: instance method body
rows.expected_post_patch: Instances created before AND after installation return 2 from v(), through direct, virtual, interface and super dispatch alike.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: The instance layout is unchanged, so pre-existing instances need no transformation to observe the new body.

rows.title: getter body
rows.expected_post_patch: Every read of .v observes the new body, including reads the optimizer turned into a direct field-like access.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: No stored shape changes; a getter is computed.

rows.title: setter body
release_sketch: class C { set v(int x) { _n = x; } int _n = 0; }
patch_sketch: class C { set v(int x) { _n = x * 2; } int _n = 0; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Every write through .v observes the new body.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Values already written by the old setter are ordinary field contents; the field's shape is unchanged.

rows.title: operator body
release_sketch: class C { int operator +(int o) => o; }
patch_sketch: class C { int operator +(int o) => o + 1; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Operator invocations observe the new body, including sites the optimizer specialized for a known receiver class.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: No state shape changes.

rows.title: factory constructor body
release_sketch: class C { factory C.make() => C._(1); C._(this.n); final int n; }
patch_sketch: class C { factory C.make() => C._(2); C._(this.n); final int n; }
rows.expected_post_patch: C.make() produces an instance built by the new body. Instances built by the old body keep the values they were built with.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Objects the old factory produced are valid instances of an unchanged layout. Retroactively rebuilding them is not implied by a body change and is not this row's claim.

rows.title: generative constructor body
release_sketch: class C { C() { n = 1; } int n = 0; }
patch_sketch: class C { C() { n = 2; } int n = 0; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Newly constructed instances run the new body. Existing instances are untouched and keep their current field values.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: The layout is unchanged. Whether existing instances SHOULD be re-initialized is a product question with no unique answer, and deliberately not promised here.

rows.title: constructor initializer list
release_sketch: class C { C() : n = 1; final int n; }
patch_sketch: class C { C() : n = 2; final int n; }
rows.expected_post_patch: New instances initialize n to 2. Final-field initialization order and semantics are preserved.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Layout unchanged; existing finals keep their values.

rows.title: redirecting factory target change
rows.expected_post_patch: C() now constructs B. Tear-offs of the redirecting factory acquired before the patch also produce B where the row's tear-off semantics apply.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Already-constructed A instances remain A instances; converting them to B is a different program change, covered by RS-01 and TS rows.

rows.title: async function body
rows.expected_post_patch: Calls started after installation complete with 2. A call already suspended inside the old body is governed by RS-05, not by this row.

rows.title: async* generator body
rows.expected_post_patch: Streams created after installation yield 2. A stream already being consumed is governed by RS-06.

rows.title: sync* generator body
rows.expected_post_patch: Iterables created after installation yield 2. A partially consumed iterator is governed by RS-06.

rows.title: closure and local function body, capture shape unchanged
release_sketch: int Function() make(int a) { return () => a + 1; }
patch_sketch: int Function() make(int a) { return () => a + 2; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Closures created after installation use the new body. A closure object created before installation, whose captured-context shape is identical, also observes the new body.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: This row is deliberately restricted to an UNCHANGED capture shape, so the context needs no transformation. A changed capture shape is RS-03 and requires its own answer.

rows.title: generic function or method body
release_sketch: T pick<T>(T a, T b) => a;
patch_sketch: T pick<T>(T a, T b) => b;
rows.expected_post_patch: Every instantiation observes the new body, including instantiations the compiler specialized or shared.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Type arguments are unchanged; only the body moved.

rows.title: extension member body
release_sketch: extension E on int { int get twice => this * 2; }
patch_sketch: extension E on int { int get twice => this * 3; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Every statically resolved extension member invocation observes the new body. Extension members are resolved statically, so this row's dispatch obligation is that static resolution is re-bound, not that a vtable is updated.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: An extension holds no instance state of its own; it is a static namespace over an existing type.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: No state shape changes.

rows.title: extension type member body
release_sketch: extension type Meters(int v) { int get cm => v * 100; }
patch_sketch: extension type Meters(int v) { int get cm => v * 1000; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Every extension type member invocation observes the new body. The erased representation is unchanged, so existing values remain valid.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: The representation type is unchanged by this row; changing it is TS-16.

rows.title: mixin member body, including mixin application stubs
rows.expected_post_patch: C().v() returns 2 through the mixin application. Every class that applies M observes the new body, including via the synthesized mixin stub.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Layout unchanged.

rows.title: callable class `call` body
rows.expected_post_patch: Both c() and c.call() observe the new body, and a Function-typed reference to an instance obtained before installation does too.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Layout unchanged.

rows.title: instance field initializer expression
rows.expected_post_patch: Instances constructed after installation start with n == 2. Existing instances keep the value they hold; changing them is a migration, not a body change.

rows.title: static or top-level lazy field initializer
rows.expected_post_patch: If x has not yet been initialized, the new initializer runs. If it HAS been initialized, its value is already observable and re-running the initializer is a state change, not a code change -- see RS-10.

rows.title: body reached through a forwarding stub or member signature
release_sketch: class B extends A { void m(covariant String s) {} }
patch_sketch: class B extends A { void m(covariant String s) { used = true; } }
rows.expected_post_patch: A call arriving through the CFE-synthesized forwarding stub reaches the new body, and the stub's covariant type check is still performed.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: No state shape changes. The stub is compiler-synthesized and must be re-derived with the member, which is a representability obligation, not a migration.

rows.title: body reached through a noSuchMethod forwarder
rows.expected_post_patch: Calls to unimplemented interface members route through the synthesized forwarder into the new noSuchMethod body.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: No state shape changes.

rows.title: extension type representation field accessor
patch_sketch: extension type Id(int value) { int get doubled => value * 2; }
rows.expected_post_patch: The synthesized representation accessor keeps working and any member added alongside it resolves; the erased representation is unchanged.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: The representation type is unchanged; changing it is TS-16.

rows.title: tear-off obtained before installation
release_sketch: final g = f; // captured before the patch
rows.expected_post_patch: Calling the previously captured tear-off g() returns 2. A tear-off is a reference to a declaration, not a snapshot of its implementation -- so a pre-patch tear-off that keeps returning 1 is a no-bypass violation, not an acceptable nuance.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: The tear-off object's own shape does not change; what it must resolve to does.

rows.title: abstract member gains a concrete body
release_sketch: class C extends A { int v() => 1; }
patch_sketch: class C extends A { int v() => 1; }
rows.expected_post_patch: A's new concrete body is reachable from subclasses that do not override, and C's override still wins for C.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: No state shape changes.

rows.title: add a top-level function
rows.expected_post_patch: Patched code may call b(). b() is resolvable by name from any patched library that imports it.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A declaration that did not exist has no prior state.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: remove a top-level function
rows.expected_post_patch: No patched call site references b(). Any surviving reference is a validation failure at patch build time, not a runtime crash.

rows.title: add a static method to an existing class
rows.expected_post_patch: C.v() resolves and executes from patched code.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A new static method holds no prior state.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: The class layout is unchanged by a static member.

rows.title: remove a static method
rows.expected_post_patch: No patched reference to C.v remains; the patch validator refuses one that does.

rows.title: add an instance method to an existing class
rows.expected_post_patch: Instances created BEFORE installation also respond to v(). A new member that only exists for newly allocated objects is a bypass.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: A method adds no storage, so no existing instance needs transformation.

rows.title: remove an instance method
rows.expected_post_patch: Calls to the removed member behave as the language specifies for a missing member (noSuchMethod), and the patch validator refuses a patch whose own code still calls it.

rows.title: add or remove a getter/setter pair
patch_sketch: class C { int n = 0; int get double_ => n * 2; set double_(int v) { n = v ~/ 2; } }
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing instances expose the new accessors.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Accessors add no storage.

rows.title: add or remove an operator
patch_sketch: class C { C operator +(C o) => this; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing instances support the new operator.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Operators add no storage.

rows.title: add or remove a generative constructor
rows.expected_post_patch: C.named() constructs a valid instance of the existing layout.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Layout unchanged.

rows.title: add or remove a factory constructor
patch_sketch: class C { C._(); factory C.make() => C._(); }
rows.expected_post_patch: C.make() resolves and constructs.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Layout unchanged.

rows.title: add a class
rows.expected_post_patch: B can be instantiated by patched code, gets a runtime class identity, participates in type tests, and its instances are collected normally.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A class that did not exist has no instances.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: remove a class
rows.expected_post_patch: No patched code references B. Live B instances must remain valid or the removal must be refused -- silently invalidating reachable objects is not acceptable.

rows.title: add or remove a mixin declaration
rows.expected_post_patch: M exists as a declaration and may be applied by patched classes. Applying it to an EXISTING class is TS-09.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A declaration that did not exist has no instances of its own.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape until it is applied, which is TS-09.

rows.title: add or remove an enum declaration
rows.expected_post_patch: E and its values exist, are canonical, compare by identity, and work in switch.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A new enum has no pre-existing values.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: add or remove an enum VALUE on an existing enum
rows.expected_post_patch: E.values reflects the new set, E.c is canonical, and enum values held by existing objects still compare identical to the corresponding new canonical values. Index-based serialization is a developer concern the contract must state rather than silently break.

rows.title: add or remove an extension declaration
patch_sketch: extension E on C { int v() => 1; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Patched code may call the extension member on existing C instances.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: An extension adds no storage to the extended type.

rows.title: add or remove an extension type declaration
rows.expected_post_patch: Id exists, erases to int, and patched code can construct and use it.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: The declaration is new and erases to an existing representation type.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: add, remove or repoint a typedef
rows.expected_post_patch: Patched code sees the new alias. Type literals and tear-offs that named the alias resolve consistently with the new definition.

rows.title: add or remove a library
rows.expected_post_patch: The new library is loadable, its declarations resolve, its privacy scope is its own, and its top-level state initializes lazily on first use.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A library that did not exist has no prior state.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: change an import, including show/hide combinators and prefixes
rows.expected_post_patch: Patched code resolves y. Name resolution is recomputed for the patched library rather than inherited from the release's resolved scope.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: Import scope is compile-time resolution, not runtime state.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: change an export surface
rows.expected_post_patch: Importers of the patched library see the new exported surface.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: Export scope is compile-time resolution, not runtime state.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: add or remove a part file
rows.expected_post_patch: Declarations in the new part belong to the enclosing library's scope and privacy, exactly as if written inline.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A part is a compile-time composition of one library.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: add, remove or change a compile-time constant
rows.expected_post_patch: Patched code reads 2. Sites where the release's optimizer FOLDED the old value must be invalidated or recompiled -- a folded constant that keeps its old value is exactly the optimizer-erased mutability #62 I3 forbids.

rows.title: add, remove or change an annotation
rows.expected_post_patch: Annotation metadata reachable at runtime reflects the new value where the release retained it; where the release discarded it, the patch may not resurrect it and must say so rather than appear to succeed.

rows.title: add or remove a STATIC field
rows.expected_post_patch: The new static field exists uninitialized and initializes lazily on first read. Removing one whose value was observed is a state loss the contract must classify, not hide.

rows.title: add a top-level variable
rows.expected_post_patch: b exists with lazy-initialization semantics and is readable and writable from patched code.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: A variable that did not exist holds no prior value.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: add an instance field to an existing class
patch_sketch: class C { int a = 1; int b = 2; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Instances allocated after installation have b. Instances that already exist must either be migrated to the new layout or observe b through an explicit versioned-layout mechanism. Reading b off an un-migrated instance may not return garbage or crash.

rows.title: remove an instance field
release_sketch: class C { int a = 1; int b = 2; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing instances lose b's storage under an explicit versioned-layout transition. The removed value is genuinely lost, which the contract states rather than implies.

rows.title: rename an instance field
rows.expected_post_patch: This is representable. Whether the old value carries into the new field is NOT determined by the code: a rename and a delete-plus-add are indistinguishable at the declaration level, so the intent must be supplied by a developer-authored migration.

rows.title: change a field's declared type
rows.expected_post_patch: New writes are checked against the new type. Existing instances may hold a value the new type rejects; that case must be refused or migrated, never silently retained as an ill-typed value.

rows.title: change nullability of a declared type
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing instances holding null must be migrated or the patch refused. A non-nullable field observed as null is a soundness break, not a nuance.

rows.title: add, remove or change a superclass
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing C instances participate in the new hierarchy: type tests against B succeed, inherited members resolve, and the field layout transition is explicit.

rows.title: add an implemented interface
patch_sketch: class C implements I { int v() => 1; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing C instances satisfy `is I` and are usable through I-typed variables and interface dispatch.

rows.title: remove an implemented interface
release_sketch: class C implements I { int v() => 1; }
rows.expected_post_patch: `is I` becomes false for existing instances too. Cached subtype results from before the patch must be invalidated, not trusted.

rows.title: add, remove or reorder a mixin application
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing C instances gain M's members and any mixin-introduced fields under an explicit layout transition. Reordering mixins changes override resolution and must take effect for existing instances.

rows.title: change generic arity of a declaration
patch_sketch: class Box<T, U> { T? v; U? w; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing Box instances carry type arguments for the OLD arity. They must be migrated to a well-formed new instantiation or observed through an explicit version, never reinterpreted positionally.

rows.title: change a generic bound
rows.expected_post_patch: New instantiations are checked against the new bound. Existing instantiations that violate it must be refused or migrated; promoted-type intersections formed under the old bound must not survive as valid.

rows.title: class/mixin declaration category transition
rows.expected_post_patch: Either the transition is representable with existing instances accounted for, or it is refused by name. A category change that silently keeps old instances under a declaration that can no longer describe them is not acceptable.

rows.title: class/enum declaration category transition
release_sketch: class E { static const a = E._(); const E._(); }
rows.expected_post_patch: Either representable with canonical identity accounted for, or refused by name. Enum values are canonical and index-bearing, so an instance that was an ordinary object cannot become one implicitly.

rows.title: abstract/concrete transition of a class
rows.expected_post_patch: New instantiation of an abstract class is rejected at patch build time. Existing instances remain valid objects.

rows.title: class modifier change (sealed/base/final/interface/mixin class)
rows.expected_post_patch: The new modifier is enforced for patched code. Exhaustiveness derived from `sealed` in the release must be re-derived rather than assumed still valid.

rows.title: extension type representation change
rows.expected_post_patch: The erasure changes, so values typed as Id under the old erasure are no longer valid. This must be refused or migrated; erasure changes are invisible at runtime and therefore the most dangerous case to leave implicit.

rows.title: function type or parameter structure change
patch_sketch: int f(int a, [int b = 0]) => a + b;
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing call sites passing the old argument shape still work where the language says they do. A pre-patch tear-off whose function type no longer matches must be handled explicitly rather than invoked with a mismatched frame.

rows.title: record type shape change
rows.expected_post_patch: New records have the new shape. Records already in the heap keep the old shape and must remain valid or be migrated; records are structurally typed, so shape is identity.

rows.title: FutureOr and union-shaped type change
rows.expected_post_patch: Callers that awaited the FutureOr still behave correctly, and type tests against the declared type reflect the new declaration.

rows.title: top, bottom and special type usage change
rows.expected_post_patch: Dynamic-invocation sites and type checks reflect the new declared type. An InvalidType surviving into an installed patch is a validation failure, never an installed program.

rows.title: existing heap instances of a changed class
release_sketch: final c = C(); // retained across the patch
patch_sketch: // C's declaration changes; c is still reachable
rows.expected_post_patch: Every reachable instance either observes the new declaration or is observed through an explicit version. No instance is left interpreting its memory under a layout that no longer describes it.

rows.title: canonicalized constants held across a patch
release_sketch: const c = C(1); // canonical instance retained
patch_sketch: // C or the const expression changes
rows.expected_post_patch: Canonical identity is preserved or explicitly re-canonicalized. Two constants that were identical must not silently become non-identical, and a constant reachable from old code must not observe a shape it cannot describe.

rows.title: closures whose capture shape changed
patch_sketch: // the closure now captures a second variable
rows.expected_post_patch: A closure object created before the patch, whose context no longer matches the new body's expectations, is migrated or observed under its own version. It is never invoked against a context shape it does not have.

rows.title: active synchronous stack frames in changed code
release_sketch: // a frame of f() is on the stack when the patch installs
rows.expected_post_patch: The already-running frame completes under a defined version -- either the old body to completion, or an explicit on-stack transition. It may not resume into a differently shaped body mid-frame.

rows.title: suspended async continuations
release_sketch: // f() is suspended at an await when the patch installs
patch_sketch: // f()'s body changes after the await point
rows.expected_post_patch: The suspended continuation resumes under a defined version. Resuming old saved state into a new body whose await points differ is forbidden; the contract must say which version wins.

rows.title: suspended generators mid-iteration
release_sketch: // a sync*/async* generator is partially consumed
rows.expected_post_patch: The partially consumed generator continues under a defined version. Yield-point identity must not shift underneath an existing iterator.

rows.title: runtime type objects and type arguments
release_sketch: final t = C; // a Type object retained across the patch
rows.expected_post_patch: Retained Type objects and instantiated TypeArguments vectors either describe the new declaration or are replaced. A stale type argument vector reinterpreted under a new arity is a memory-safety failure, not a semantic nuance.

rows.title: subtype test caches
release_sketch: // `x is I` executed many times, result cached
patch_sketch: // the hierarchy changes so the answer changes
rows.expected_post_patch: Every subtype cache whose answer the patch invalidates is cleared or versioned. A cached `true` surviving an interface removal is a no-bypass violation.

rows.title: inline caches and dispatch specialization state
release_sketch: // a call site is monomorphic and hot before the patch
rows.expected_post_patch: Every cached dispatch target that the patch supersedes is invalidated. A hot monomorphic site continuing to call the old target is precisely the bypass #62 I2 forbids, and is not excused by being rare.

rows.title: static and top-level field state across a patch
release_sketch: int counter = 0; // mutated at runtime before the patch
patch_sketch: int counter = 0; // same declaration, new program version
rows.expected_post_patch: An already-initialized static keeps its runtime value; it is not silently reset to the initializer. A newly added static is uninitialized and initializes lazily. Which of the two applies must be decidable from the declaration identity, not from initialization order.

rows.title: library, namespace and program metadata state
release_sketch: // the release's library set and resolved namespaces
patch_sketch: // a patch adds a library and changes an import
rows.expected_post_patch: The runtime library set is updated as one transition. Name resolution, privacy scope and library identity stay consistent, and a half-registered library is never observable.

rows.title: declaration-to-implementation binding
release_sketch: // the release's Function objects bound to release Code
patch_sketch: // the patch supplies a replacement implementation
rows.expected_post_patch: The binding from a stable declaration identity to its current implementation is the single point of truth, and switching it is what installation means. Any path that reaches an implementation without consulting it is a bypass.

rows.title: isolates and isolate-spawn behaviour
release_sketch: // a long-lived spawned isolate exists at install time
patch_sketch: // code that both isolates execute changes
rows.expected_post_patch: Every isolate in the group observes one program version, or the versions each observes are explicit. Two isolates silently running different program versions is a correctness defect, and message shapes must remain compatible across the transition.

rows.title: existing record instances
release_sketch: final r = (1, 'a'); // retained across the patch
patch_sketch: // the producing code now builds a different shape
rows.expected_post_patch: Records already in the heap keep their shape and stay readable. Records are structural, so a shape change makes a new type rather than modifying the old one, and both must be describable at once.

rows.title: deferred loading units
release_sketch: import 'b.dart' deferred as b; // not yet loaded
patch_sketch: // code inside the deferred unit changes
rows.expected_post_patch: A deferred unit loaded after installation carries the patched code. A unit already loaded observes the patch like any other code. A unit never loaded does not make the patch appear installed when it is not.

rows.title: stable declaration identity, including library-private names
rows.expected_post_patch: A declaration that survives an edit keeps one identity across release and patch compilation, and a library-private name binds to the same library it did in the release. Identity may not derive from machine-code addresses, object-pool offsets, transient class ids, declaration ordering, absolute paths or temporary directories.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: Identity is the precondition for every migration, not itself a state transformation. If identity is wrong, no migration can be correct -- which is why this row gates the others rather than depending on them.

rows.title: StatefulWidget build method change
rows.expected_post_patch: The next build of an EXISTING element produces the new tree. No process restart and no root remount is required, and neither may be used to make this row pass.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: A build method holds no state; the State object's fields are FL-02.

rows.title: State subclass field set change
patch_sketch: class _S extends State<W> { int n = 0; String s = ''; }
rows.expected_post_patch: Mounted State objects gain the new field under the layout transition of TS-01, keeping the values they already hold. Silently discarding live UI state is a failure, not an acceptable simplification.

rows.title: State lifecycle method change
rows.expected_post_patch: Elements mounted after installation run the new lifecycle body. Already-mounted elements do not re-run initState, and the contract says so rather than leaving it to chance.

rows.title: InheritedWidget change and dependent notification
release_sketch: bool updateShouldNotify(covariant I old) => value != old.value;
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing dependents registered before installation observe the new notification behaviour.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: The dependency registry's shape does not change; only the predicate does.

rows.title: Dart-implemented RenderObject change
rows.expected_post_patch: Existing render objects in the live tree use the new layout and paint bodies on the next frame, with correct dirtying.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: No field shape changes in this row; a render object that gains fields is TS-01 plus FL-02.

rows.title: framework-private Dart member change
rows.expected_post_patch: Framework Dart code is patchable on the same terms as application Dart code, including library-private members, with library-bound privacy preserved.

axis_notes.semantic_migration: This row is a body change; framework state shape changes fall under the TS and RS rows.

rows.title: generated Dart plugin registrant change
release_sketch: // GeneratedPluginRegistrant registers plugins A and B
rows.expected_post_patch: The Dart half of plugin registration is patchable. Adding a plugin whose NATIVE half is not in the shipped binary is out of scope and must be refused by name rather than half-applied.

rows.title: Dart-only package graph change
patch_sketch: // app adds a dependency on a Dart-only package
rows.expected_post_patch: New Dart-only package libraries load and resolve. A package with a native component is out of scope and refused by name.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: Newly added libraries have no prior state in the process.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Nothing existing changes shape.

rows.title: const widget canonicalization across a patch
release_sketch: const Text('a') // canonical, used as an element identity input
rows.expected_post_patch: Widget equality and element reuse behave per the framework's rules under the new constants. A stale canonical const causing an element not to rebuild is a failure of RS-02 surfacing as a UI defect.

rows.title: widget type or key change affecting element reuse
rows.expected_post_patch: The framework's own reuse rules apply unchanged: a different runtime type unmounts and remounts, and State is discarded exactly where Flutter says it should be. The patch mechanism must not add reuse the framework would not do, nor destroy reuse it would.

rows.title: in-flight framework async work across installation
release_sketch: // an animation ticker and a pending Future are live
rows.expected_post_patch: Tickers, scheduled frame callbacks and pending Futures registered before installation resolve under a defined version rather than being dropped or double-run.

rows.title: arbitrary Dart-only change to a representative Flutter application
release_sketch: // a real multi-screen Flutter app at release
patch_sketch: // an arbitrary Dart-only edit across several libraries
rows.expected_post_patch: The composite case: an arbitrary Dart-only edit applies to a running app under a fixed native binary. This row may only be PROVEN when every row it composes is PROVEN, so it can never be the first row to go green.

rows.title: any statement, expression, pattern or initializer inside a replaced body
release_sketch: int f(Object o) { if (o is int) return o; return 0; }
patch_sketch: int f(Object o) => switch (o) { int i => i, _ => 0 };
rows.expected_post_patch: The contents of a body are not enumerated one construct at a time: a body is replaced wholesale, so every statement, expression, pattern and initializer node is covered by whichever body row owns the enclosing declaration. This blanket is written down so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight -- and it is genuinely one rule, because no body-content node has patch semantics independent of the declaration containing it.

axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: Body content is code, not state. State reached by that code belongs to the RS rows.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: Replacing a body changes no state shape by itself.

rows.title: program structure containers
release_sketch: // Component, Source and Location as emitted for the release
patch_sketch: // the same containers re-emitted for the patch
rows.expected_post_patch: Program-level containers are re-emitted per compilation and carry no patch semantics of their own; what matters is that the identities they hold (ID-01) and the libraries they contain (DA-19, RS-11) are correct.

axis_notes.dispatch_correctness: A container is never a call target.
axis_notes.live_state_compatibility: These are compilation artifacts, not runtime state.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: No developer-visible state shape.

rows.title: abstract kernel node base types
release_sketch: // Node, TreeNode, NamedNode and the marker interfaces
patch_sketch: // unchanged; these are never instantiated as themselves
rows.expected_post_patch: Abstract bases and marker interfaces are not program constructs a developer edits. Their obligations are discharged by the concrete rows that extend them, and they appear here so the universe is fully accounted for.

axis_notes.dispatch_correctness: An abstract base node is never itself a call target.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: No developer-visible state shape.

rows.title: kernel serialization and implementation helpers
release_sketch: // BinarySink, BinarySource and internal list helpers
patch_sketch: // unchanged by any Dart program edit
rows.expected_post_patch: These types implement kernel serialization and have no correspondence to any Dart construct a developer can write. They carry no patch semantics; the obligation they imply is that patch kernel is serialized and deserialized correctly, which is the patch toolchain's job and is gated at MAOT-13.

axis_notes.dispatch_correctness: Not a call target in the patched program.
axis_notes.semantic_migration: No developer-visible state shape.
